ORDER Heard with the aid of case diary.

This is second application filed under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (in short "BNSS"), for grant of bail to the applicant/accused, relating to FIR/Crime No.11/2023 dated (not mentioned) registered at Police Station - Mahila Police Thana, District - Mandsaur (M.P.)
for commission of offence punishable under Sections 376-D, 506 and 34 of IPC.
2.

entities.text: Police Station - Mahila Police Thana, District - Mandsaur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The first application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 26.02.2024 passed in MCRC No.8015/2024.
3. Prosecution story, in brief is that, on 19.09.2023, at around 02:30 - 03:00 AM, when the prosecutrix and her three minor children under 09 years of age were sleeping in their room, cooler was on.
Husband of the 2 MCRC-30742-2024 prosecutrix was also not available in the house.
Someone rang the doorbell.
Then, the prosecutrix opened the door and saw that co-accused Salman Sunni was there.
He caught hold her.
Then, applicant Adil Koka and co-accused Jafar @ Kala also came there.
Both of them tied her both hands by rope, then went out of the room.
Co-accused Salman tied her mouth by cloth.
Thereafter, he committed rape upon her and threatened that if she will tell the incident to someone, he will kill her.
After the incident, she called her relatives and narrated the incident.
In the morning of next day, husband of the prosecutrix returned home.
She also narrated the incident to her husband and matter was reported on the same day against the applicant and co- accused persons.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant/accused submits that the applicant has not committed the offence and he has falsely been implicated in the case.

It is submitted that after dismissal of first bail application of the applicant as withdrawn, the prosecutrix (PW-1) and Doctor Manish Bajya (PW-2),
who conducted MLC of the prosecutrix have been examined before the trial Court.
It is also submitted that however the prosecutrix supported the case of prosecution, but there are material contradictions and omissions in her statement.
5. It is further submitted that there is also contradictions between the statement of prosecutrix (PW-1) and Dr. Manish Bajya (PW-2).
As per statement of Dr. Manish Bajya, no sign of struggle was found on body of the prosecutrix.
The FIR was lodged belatedly by 11 hours without any cogent 3 MCRC-30742-2024 explanation.
As alleged, three minor children were sleeping alongwith the prosecutrix.
Therefore, it was not possible to commit rape with the prosecutrix by the co-accused.
The prosecution case is doubtful.
Applicant is in custody since 19.09.2023.
Conclusion of trial will take considerable long time for its disposal, therefore, it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.
6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the non-applicant/State has opposed the prayer and submits that the prosecutrix has fully supported the case of prosecution in her statement.
There are no material contradictions and omissions in her statement.

The offence is serious in nature,
therefore he is not entitled for bail.
7. Having heard learned counsel for the parties, perused the case-diary also considering the facts and circumstances of the case, at this stage, I am not inclined to grant bail to the applicant.
Resultantly, application for bail is rejected.

(PRAKASH CHANDRA GUPTA) JUDGE Shruti Aadil Koka vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118622493/
